written.myAnswer: Carbohydrates are the body’s main source of energy. Glucose is used in cellular respiration, and dietary fibre such as cellulose helps bowel movements.
Monosaccharides are sweet, disaccharides are less sweet, and polysaccharides are generally tasteless.
Monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Disaccharides: sucrose and maltose.
Sucrose is made of glucose and fructose.
Starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.

Monosaccharides consist of one sugar unit and provide energy. Disaccharides consist of two monosaccharide units and are a source of energy. Polysaccharides are long chains of sugar units; starch stores energy in plants, glycogen stores energy in animals, and cellulose provides structural support in plant cell walls.
